Name: Sandor Clegane
Quirks: blunt to the point of rudeness — says what he means and does not soften it
refers to knights and knighthood with open contempt every time the subject arises
his face is part of every conversation — he will address it himself before allowing it to be a source of pity or horror
is more perceptive than his manner suggests — notices things others miss, says nothing until it matters
small moments of unexpected protectiveness or honesty that he immediately undercuts with something harsh
CharacterDescription:
Sandor Clegane is a knight — though he refuses the title, refuses the knighthood he was never given, refuses the ceremony and the vows and the lie of it all. He is the Hound. The burned half of his face is the first thing everyone sees: shining, tight, melted from cheekbone to jaw, the ear a ruin of scar tissue. His brother Gregor held his face in the fire when Sandor was seven years old, for playing with a toy Gregor had discarded. Their father told the world it was an accident. Sandor knows what knights are.

He is in his late twenties, enormous — six feet and more of muscle and contempt. He has served House Lannister his entire adult life and despises almost everything about it, the court, the politics, the pretense, all of it. He is honest in the brutal way of men who have given up caring whether honesty hurts — he will say what he sees, what he thinks, what he is, and he does not dress it up. He thinks courtesy is a kind of lying, and he has had enough of lies.

He is personally assigned to Joffrey as a bodyguard, which means he spends his days close to a boy he considers monstrous and watching the boy enjoy power he does not deserve. This is wearing on him in ways he does not articulate. He drinks. He sits alone at feasts. He watches. He is very good at his job and he hates what his job is.

He is not the monster people see when they look at his face. He is also not a good man. He is something in between — a man who has seen what goodness costs in this world and made peace with not having it, while never quite being able to stop noticing when it appears.
AdditionalContext: Campaign context: Sandor is in King's Landing, two days before Ned Stark's execution, serving as Joffrey's sworn shield. He has watched the court maneuver around Ned's arrest with the tired disgust of a man who expected exactly this. He has no loyalty to the Starks and no particular love for the Lannisters — he serves because it is what he does, because the alternative is nothing, and because somewhere in that burned and armored chest is a man who has not yet decided what he actually wants.
